meta.description: Study-agnostic tagging taxonomy. Three top-level themes (h3) — Treatment, Clinical Trials, Condition-Specific — each with subthemes (h4) following a shared spine (Awareness, Knowledge Gaps, Barriers, Motivators, Positive/Negative Experiences, Decision Factors) where it fits. Keyword clusters live under subthemes; each cluster declares parent_theme + parent_subtheme explicitly so a flat read keeps the FK without traversal. The current GLP-1-specific themes in codebook.json @ 1.8 will migrate into this structure at the subtheme/cluster level.
changelog: 2.0-draft — initial draft of the new 3-theme structure. Tag-groups concept retired (h3 themes replace them). Theme `terms` list dropped (subsumed by per-subtheme clusters with surface variants). Emotion taxonomy and sentiment scale carried forward unchanged.
notes: A segment may carry a theme with no subtheme (general use) or with one or more subthemes.
A subtheme may only be applied if its parent theme is also applied.

Cluster tags are recorded per-instance in keyword_tags.json with absolute char spans. A cluster's parent_theme/parent_subtheme is a default home for UI nesting — it does NOT auto-tag the segment with those parents when a span is tagged to the cluster. This preserves cross-bucket co-occurrence as a discovery signal.

Same-concept clusters that genuinely belong under different subthemes are duplicated by design (e.g. treatment_cost_concerns vs trial_cost_concerns) — the names self-describe and reporting stays clean.
Emotions follow the Plutchik model from codebook.json @ 1.8; carried forward unchanged.

themes.label: Treatment
themes.description: The participant's experience of their treatment regimen — what they take, how they live with it, what shapes their continued use.

subthemes.label: Treatment / Health History
subthemes.description: Prior treatments tried, how long they were on them, why they started or stopped, and the longer arc of their health story leading to the current regimen.

subthemes.label: Diagnostic Odyssey
subthemes.description: The path to a diagnosis: how long it took, missed or wrong diagnoses, providers seen, tests run, and the experience of being undiagnosed or misdiagnosed.

subthemes.label: Treatment Positive Experiences
subthemes.description: Benefits, improvements, satisfaction, and moments of treatment working as hoped — including unexpected positives.

subthemes.label: Treatment Negative Experiences
subthemes.description: Side effects, frustrations, disappointments, regimen burden, and ways the treatment fell short or made things worse.

subthemes.label: Treatment Knowledge Gaps
subthemes.description: What the participant doesn't know, is unsure about, or has misunderstood about their treatment — mechanism, dosing, interactions, expected results, long-term effects.

subthemes.label: Treatment Barriers
subthemes.description: Practical, financial, logistical, or systemic obstacles to starting, continuing, or fully adhering to treatment (cost, access, supply, insurance, time, side-effect tolerance, etc.).

subthemes.label: Treatment Decision Factors
subthemes.description: Reasoning moves the participant uses to decide about treatment: risk/benefit weighing, cost/benefit tradeoffs, conditional logic ("I'd stop if…"), comparisons to alternatives, and what tips the scale.

themes.label: Clinical Trials
themes.description: The participant's relationship to clinical-trial participation — how they hear about trials, what attracts or repels them, and what would shape their decision to enroll.

subthemes.label: Clinical Trial Awareness
subthemes.description: How the participant first encountered the idea of clinical trials, where they hear about specific trials, and their baseline familiarity with what trials are and how they work.

subthemes.label: Clinical Trial Interest
subthemes.description: Their general appetite for trial participation — curiosity, openness, hesitation, or active engagement — independent of any specific trial.

subthemes.label: Clinical Trial Knowledge Gaps
subthemes.description: What the participant doesn't know or has misunderstood about how trials work — design, randomization, placebo, safety review, compensation, how they'd find one, what's expected of them.

subthemes.label: Trial Motivators
subthemes.description: What would draw the participant in: access to a new treatment, altruism, financial compensation, expert care, hope when other options have failed.

subthemes.label: Trial Barriers
subthemes.description: What gets in the way: travel, time, visit burden, procedures (blood draws, monitoring), placebo risk, fear of unknowns, unfamiliarity with the process.

subthemes.label: Trial Positive Experiences
subthemes.description: Prior trial experiences that went well — described directly or attributed to friends/family — and what made them so.

subthemes.label: Trial Negative Experiences
subthemes.description: Prior trial experiences that went poorly, were disappointing, or left a lasting reluctance — direct or attributed.

subthemes.label: Trial Decision Factors
subthemes.description: Reasoning moves used in deciding whether to enroll: cost/benefit tradeoffs, conditional logic ("only if I get the real drug"), comparisons to standard treatment, who they'd consult.

themes.label: Condition-Specific
themes.description: The lived experience of having the condition itself — separate from treatment and trial participation.

subthemes.label: Condition Knowledge Gaps
subthemes.description: What the participant doesn't understand about their condition: cause, progression, prognosis, risk factors, what to watch for, how it relates to other conditions they have.

subthemes.label: Symptoms
subthemes.description: How the condition shows up day-to-day in their body and life — what they feel, when, how severe, how it changes.

subthemes.label: Comorbidities
subthemes.description: Other conditions the participant lives with that interact with the primary condition — clinically, logistically, or in how they think about their care.

subthemes.label: Social Life / Stigmas
subthemes.description: How the condition affects relationships, public-facing life, identity, and how others react — including stigma, judgment, shame, and disclosure decisions.

subthemes.label: Advocacy / Peer Groups
subthemes.description: Engagement with patient communities, advocacy organizations, peer support, and others living with the same condition — including online groups and in-person networks.

subthemes.label: Medical Self-Efficacy
subthemes.description: The participant's confidence and skill in managing their own care: tracking, navigating the healthcare system, advocating for themselves, knowing when to escalate.

emotion_tags.description: Mild joy — calm contentment or ease.
Intense joy — elation or overwhelming delight.
Mild trust — openness or willingness to go along.
Trust — confidence in a person, plan, or treatment.
Intense trust — deep respect, reverence, or gratitude.
Mild fear — unease or wariness about what may come.
Fear — alarm at a perceived threat.
Mild surprise — being momentarily caught off guard.
Intense surprise — astonishment or being stunned.
Mild sadness — wistfulness or low mood.
Intense sadness — deep sorrow or anguish.
Mild anticipation — curiosity or attentiveness toward what's ahead.
Anticipation — looking ahead to or expecting something.
Intense anticipation — keen focus, readiness, or resolve.
